title: Integration discovery - Zenith Solutions
summary: Discovery call to understand Zenith's integration needs for Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Main points: they use LangChain in prod, evaluate LlamaIndex for retrieval augmentation, need a gateway/proxy approach for routing and auth, are sensitive to rate limits and per-token cost, want observability hooks and token-level tracing, and have strong compliance requirements (SAML, KMS, audit logs). Next steps: send pricing + dedicated config, infra runbook for VPC, and plan a short technical POC for LangChain integration and benchmark sample prompts.
action_items: Maya - send pricing sheet and Dedicated tiers by 2026-07-03
Sanjay - share SDK quickstart and LangChain example repo by 2026-07-02
Omar - provide 3 sample prompt workloads and expected rps by 2026-07-05
Priya - circulate internal security checklist and responsible sec contacts by 2026-07-04
next_steps: Schedule 2-hour technical POC session (SE-led) w/ sample prompts and latency benchmarks
Provide VPC deployment runbook + KMS integration notes
Customer to confirm timeline and pilot scope by next week
header: Date: 2026-07-01 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~50m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Sanjay Patel (Redwood SE), Lara Kim (CTO, Zenith), Omar Ruiz (Lead ML Eng, Zenith), Priya Desai (Platform Eng, Zenith)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro, I'm Maya, AE on the Redwood side. Sanjay is our SE - he'll cover technical bits.
[00:07] Lara Kim: Hi Maya, thanks. I'm Lara. Omar and Priya are with me. We run the ML platform at Zenith.
[00:12] Sanjay Patel: Hi all. Quick agenda, we'll go over your current stack, integration patterns (SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex), then deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), and finish with next steps.
[00:28] Lara Kim: Sounds good. For context, we've been prototyping several LLM features in our product — conversational search and auto-responses. We're heavy on LangChain right now, and evaluating LlamaIndex for our retrieval layer.
[00:40] Omar Ruiz: Our infra is k8s, internal api gateway, and we have a proxy pattern for model calls today. We want to centralize observability and limit per-team throughput.
[00:50] Priya Desai: Important: we need SOC2 compliance, SAML SSO, and customer data encryption with our KMS — and many of our customers demand data residency controls.
[01:05] Maya Chen: Totally. Those are common asks. Quick question: when you say proxy pattern, is that an internal gateway that authenticates and forwards requests to model endpoints?
[01:14] Omar Ruiz: Yeah, we have a small gateway that handles routing, rate limiting, and some prompt templating. We're thinking about moving to Redwood for the model side but keeping our gateway for auth and per-tenant quotas.
[01:26] Sanjay Patel: That model fits well — Redwood supports a gateway/proxy approach. You can keep your auth/routing layer and call Redwood's Hosted API, or if you need isolation and VPC, we can deploy Redwood Private into your VPC or provide Dedicated capacity with private networking options.
[01:42] Lara Kim: Question on SDKs — we have Python microservices and some Node ingestion workers. How mature are Redwood SDKs and examples for LangChain / LlamaIndex?
[01:51] Sanjay Patel: We have official Python and Node SDKs, plus LangChain connectors and community examples for LlamaIndex. I'll drop the quickstart repo. The LangChain wrappers handle streaming tokens and function calling. There are sometimes naming mismatches in the auto-transcripts — people call the package redwood-client in code examples.
[02:10] Omar Ruiz: Ok. How does streaming interact with our gateway? We do prompt streaming to the client and also need token-level cost attribution per tenant.
[02:19] Sanjay Patel: You can stream through Redwood back to your gateway — our API supports chunked responses and server-sent events/streaming websockets. For cost attribution we surface token-level metrics per API key and per-route in the Console and via our observability hooks. You can tag requests with metadata (tenant id) and get per-tenant breakdowns.
[02:37] Priya Desai: Rate limits are critical — we have bursty traffic and need hard quotas per-tenant. Can we enforce rate limits at the gateway and have Redwood apply quotas so we don't exceed budget?
[02:48] Maya Chen: Yes — typically customers enforce coarse rate limiting at the gateway and rely on Redwood's quota management for billing and hard caps. Redwood supports per-key quotas, soft and hard limits, and alerts. We can also propose autoscale/burst policies on Dedicated capacity.
[03:05] Lara Kim: On Private deployment — is there an on-prem option? Some of our regulated customers require air-gapped setups.
[03:12] Sanjay Patel: We have Private (VPC and an on-prem package). On-prem has a slightly longer onboarding — we'd need to run a small appliance or VM image, integrate with your KMS/HSM, and set up secure links for the control plane. For VPC we host the control plane while compute lives in your cloud VPC.
[03:29] Omar Ruiz: KMS integration — do you rotate keys? Audit logs? We need proof of key separation and audit trails.
[03:36] Maya Chen: Yes, we integrate with major KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and can provide HSM-backed options for Private. We also expose audit logs and per-request metadata for compliance and forensics.
[03:49] Priya Desai: Observability hooks — we want tracing across our services into Redwood. Can we add our trace ids and have them show up in the Console?
[03:58] Sanjay Patel: Absolutely. You can pass trace headers and request ids, and they'll be associated with tokens and latencies in the Console. We also have an events API to stream logs to your SIEM or to forward traces to Datadog/Scalyr.
[04:11] Lara Kim: Latency vs cost tradeoff — we care about p99 latency for chat flows. What options have customers used?
[04:18] Sanjay Patel: For p99 low latency, Dedicated capacity with reserved GPU pools is common. You can pin model variants (smaller quantized models) for latency-sensitive routes and fall back to higher-quality variants when latency slack exists. We also do prefix KV caching to reduce repeated context compute.
[04:35] Omar Ruiz: Are there recommended quantization profiles? We saw mixed perf on small GPUs.
[04:41] Sanjay Patel: We provide model and quantization recommendations per workload. For sequence lengths and batch sizes like yours (you gave a rough rps earlier), we'd probably suggest an int8 quantized variant for latency-sensitive endpoints. We'll include the perf matrix in the follow-up.
[04:56] Maya Chen: Quick ops question — deployment rollouts and canaries? We need to be able to A/B test model versions and rollback automatically on regressions.
[05:04] Sanjay Patel: Rollouts are supported — canary percent traffic, A/B tests, automatic fallback to previous model if latency or error thresholds exceed SLOs. You can integrate evaluation triggers based on your prompt sets too.
[05:18] Priya Desai: For integration, we use LangChain in production with a custom retriever. How invasive is the integration with LlamaIndex? Could we keep our vector store and only replace the model endpoint?
[05:28] Sanjay Patel: You can absolutely keep your vector store. LlamaIndex and LangChain are both agnostic to the model endpoint — just configure the Redwood SDK as the llm/client. For retrieval augmentation, we recommend passing the retrieved docs in the context and use our structured output support for safe parsing. We'll include a sample LangChain wrapper showing how to swap in Redwood with minimal code changes.
[05:45] Lara Kim: Pricing question — hosted per-token pricing vs Dedicated commits — our CFO will want rough numbers for a pilot of ~5M tokens/month.
[05:53] Maya Chen: I'll send a pricing estimate for hosted and for a small Dedicated commitment. Hosted is easier to start; Dedicated gives predictable unit cost. We'll include break-even analysis for your workload.
[06:03] Omar Ruiz: Thinking about SLOs — what uptime / latency SLAs do you offer for Dedicated?
[06:08] Maya Chen: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; we'll include the SLA document and describe regional fallbacks. For Hosted we have best-effort public metrics and tiers.
[06:18] Priya Desai: Security review — we'll need SOC2, incident response, penetration test reports.
[06:24] Maya Chen: We'll share our security pack and are happy to arrange a compliance call with our security team; some customers sign an NDA prior to getting full reports.
[06:33] Lara Kim: Ok, let's talk POC scope. We want a LangChain-based demo with retrieval-augmented generation, about 200 rps peak, typical prompt sizes around 1k tokens, occasional longer contexts. We want p95 < 400ms.
[06:45] Sanjay Patel: That helps. For that profile, we'll propose either a small Dedicated pool with an int8 model variant and prefix caching, or test Hosted with aggressive autoscale and caching — the POC will validate p95.
[06:56] Omar Ruiz: How about SDK auth? We need to route tenant tokens via our gateway and then spike down to a single Redwood API key per environment, while still getting per-tenant metrics. Is that supported?
[07:06] Sanjay Patel: Yes — you can forward tenant ids as metadata and tag usage server-side. We support token exchange patterns: short-lived keys and meta-headers that preserve attribution.
[07:16] Priya Desai: Any gotchas with function calling and structured outputs? We rely on JSON outputs for actions and need a robust parse layer.
[07:24] Sanjay Patel: Structured output support is included; function calling is supported in streaming modes. There are occasional tokenizer edge cases we can help debug. We also have result validators and schema checks you can enable.
[07:36] Lara Kim: Great. A couple of minor points — can we route sensitive prompts to Private while keeping lower-sensitivity requests on Hosted to save cost?
[07:45] Maya Chen: Yes — routing policies can send requests by tag to Hosted, Dedicated, or Private model variants. Automatic fallback is also possible if capacity is constrained.
[07:55] Omar Ruiz: For the POC, what do you need from us?
[07:58] Sanjay Patel: 1) sample prompt set and expected rps, 2) access to a staging environment or to run the gateway proxy, 3) goals for latency/quality, and 4) a contact for our technical POC session.
[08:10] Lara Kim: We'll get you the sample prompts and a staging token.
[08:14] Maya Chen: Perfect. We'll follow up with the resources and links.
[08:17] (brief audio overlap)
[08:20] Priya Desai: One more question on observability exports — do you have a webhook or a streaming API? We want to stream token-level events into our ELK.
[08:28] Sanjay Patel: We have an events API and can stream to a customer endpoint; some customers use an AWS Kinesis or Kafka sink. We'll include the events schema.
[08:36] Lara Kim: Awesome. Any security pre-reqs for VPC option?
[08:39] Maya Chen: We'll provide a VPC runbook with required peering, firewall rules, and IAM roles. For on-prem we'll need a network jump-host and some outbound egress for updates.
[08:52] Omar Ruiz: Last thing — are there rate-limit headers returned for programmatic backoff?
[08:56] Sanjay Patel: Yes, standard headers and retry-after on 429s; we also support a webhook for near-capacity alerts.
[09:04] Lara Kim: Ok that covers most of it. Thanks.
[09:07] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. To recap next steps — Maya will send pricing and SLA docs, Sanjay will share SDKs and LangChain examples, and we'll schedule the SE-led POC.
[09:18] Lara Kim: Sounds good. We'll aim to respond with sample prompts by Monday.
[09:22] (call ends)
notes: Customer uses LangChain in prod and is evaluating LlamaIndex
They have an internal gateway/proxy and want to preserve tenant-level auth and quotas
Priority: p95/p99 latency for chat flows; SOC2/KMS/SAML requirements
POC will validate latency and token-level billing attribution
